comment: STANDING DELIVERIES (v7). The subscriptions and scheduled drops that keep arriving
whether or not anyone is home — the thing a home-away goal has to deal with before it
can claim the house is ready.
WHY THIS IS ITS OWN FILE AND NOT A FIELD ON shopping_list.json. A shopping list is
what the family intends to buy; these are commitments already made to third parties.
Holding one is an outward-facing act with a date attached, and Deliveries.Hold is
graded A2 precisely because of that — it is not the same kind of thing as adding milk
to a list, and folding it into ShoppingList would have made one plugin mean two
things and one grade cover both.
ESSENTIAL vs NOT is the household's call, recorded here rather than inferred. The
planner is told which is which; it does not get to decide that the medication drop is
non-essential because nobody will be in.
See data/README.md for the generic-clock rule: `every_days` is a cadence and
`next_in_days` resolves against IClock.Today at read time, so 'the next one' is always
correctly in the future however long the seed sits here.
RUNTIME-MUTATED: Hold and Resume write `held` and `held_until` back. Restore from git
